ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.74 Ryde voucher to the rider for the un-exempted second off-route segment (F4), and remind the driver that any route change after the initial agreement requires a fresh rider agreement before leaving the optimal route.
ruling.reasoning:
Rider's complaint: she agreed to go round the jam at the start, but the driver later deviated a second time without asking; she wants that part refunded. The trip is RydeTAXI, so the fare is metered and extra kilometres enter the fare: total charged $61.32 with an excess-distance line of $14.64 for 10.38 km at $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2].

Two off-route segments are measured: F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) and F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) [F1][F3][F4]. Neither has a qualifying traffic incident — F15 records no incidents, and the speed-band facts F13/F14 are band 4, which under RD-4(b) is at most corroborative and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Segment F3: the driver asked at 18:42, “Traffic ahead on Bukit Timah Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?” and the rider replied at 18:43, “Sure, your call.” [F9][F10]. The chat record is complete with two timestamped messages, so the agreement is before the segment start of 18:46 [F11][RD-5]. Reading the rider's words in context, she accepted the driver's proposed route rather than exercising a general “whichever way is faster” licence — the proposal named a specific route, and “your call” leaves the route choice to the driver within what he proposed [F9][F10]. No record ties the driven path to Rifle Range Road, but nothing places it elsewhere either (the driver's post-trip statement does not name another road for this segment and is not consent evidence in any event) [F12]. On this reading and the absent road-name tie, I leave F3 undetermined rather than exempt [RD-5][RD-3]. Because F3 alone would add 5.66 km × $1.4100/km = $7.98 to the refund if counted, this undetermined finding changes the amount, so its share is not refunded and goes to the human reviewer alongside the ruling [F3][F5][RD-2].

Segment F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) is different: the only rider message is at 18:43, twenty minutes before this segment began [F10][F11]. A message that early, read in context, cannot cover a turn-off taken at 19:03, and RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be sent before the segment it covers [F10][RD-5]. The driver's statement that “the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting” is his own account written after the trip and is not rider consent [F12]. F4 therefore counts as an un-exempted deviation and its extra kilometres are refundable under the metered fare model [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: $43.64 distance fare ÷ 30.95 km = $1.4100/km, the trace rate; 4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.74 [F5][F8][RD-2]. This is a non-cash voucher refund under NS-7 [RD-2][NS-7]. F18 shows no prior upheld route dispute, so RD-6's repeated-breach condition is not met and no account flag is raised [F18][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the chat (F9, F10), the driver's statement (F12) and the complaint; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient for the F4 ruling: the fare record gives the rate and the segment's extra km, the chat record is complete and timestamped, and the deviation measurements are fixed [F3][F4][F5][F8][F11].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 18:43 message “Sure, your call” replies to the driver's proposal to go round via Rifle Range Road, sent before the segment start of 18:46 on a complete timestamped chat record [F9][F10][F11]. No fact ties the driven path of F3 to Rifle Range Road, and nothing places it elsewhere (the driver's post-trip statement does not name another road for this segment and is not consent) [F12]. Under RD-5 + G13 a named-road agreement untied to the driven segment is undetermined; because this finding changes the amount, that share goes to a human reviewer while the settled portion (F4) is refunded [F3][RD-5].

The only rider message is at 18:43, roughly twenty minutes before this segment began at 19:03, and read in context it cannot cover a later second turn-off; RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be sent before the segment it covers [F10][F11][RD-5]. The driver's statement that “the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting” is his own post-trip account and is not rider consent [F12]. The segment therefore counts as an un-exempted deviation whose extra km are refundable under the metered fare model [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: confirm whether the first off-route segment (F3, 18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) is covered by the rider's 18:43 reply to the Rifle Range Road proposal before it began (F9, F10), since the fare formula turns on that segment; the second segment (F4, 19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) is settled as un-exempted.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a route deviation on a RydeTAXI trip: total charged $61.32, with an excess-distance line of $14.64 for 10.38 km at $1.4100/km, so extra kilometres enter the fare [F5][F8][RD-2]. Two off-route segments exist under RD-1: F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) and F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) [F1][F3][F4].

Neither segment has a qualifying incident: no traffic incident is recorded, and the Bukit Timah Expressway / Pan Island Expressway speed-band facts show band 4 (30–39 km/h), which under RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

For F3 the code trace leaves the RD-5 scope question open. At 18:42 the driver proposed going round the jam via Rifle Range Road and the rider replied at 18:43, “Sure, your call.” — before the 18:46 segment start, on a complete timestamped chat record [F9][F10][F11]. Nothing in the fact table ties the driven path of F3 to Rifle Range Road, and nothing places it elsewhere either; the driver's post-trip assertion that “the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting” is his own account and cannot supply rider consent [F12]. Under RD-5 with G13, an agreed named road untied to the driven segment is undetermined, and because F3's 5.66 km × $1.4100/km ≈ $7.98 would change the refund amount, this undetermined finding must go to a person rather than be decided by me [F3][F5][RD-5].

For F4 the only rider message is at 18:43, twenty minutes before the 19:03 segment, and read in context it cannot cover a later second turn-off; RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be sent before the segment it covers, so F4 counts as an un-exempted deviation [F10][F11][F12][F4][RD-1][RD-5]. Its extra km would be refundable, but with F3 undetermined the total cannot be fixed to the cent, so no amount is stated here [F4][F5][RD-2].

F18 records no prior upheld route dispute, so the repeated-breach condition of RD-6 is not met and no account flag is raised [F18][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the chat (F9, F10), the driver's statement (F12) and the complaint, and found no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. Evidence is otherwise complete (GPS segments, fare record, full timestamped chat), the gap being only the road-name tie for F3 [F3][F4][F5][F8][F11].
